title: Tail decoding run
statement: Let $z$ and $t$ be finite bit strings, let $h=angle z,trangle$, and set $p=2|z|+2$. For either Boolean mode, if $t$ is canonical and $|t|$ is at most the length of the binary representation of $|h|$, the machine has a run from the configuration with state $mathrm{copy}(0,mathrm{false})$, pointer $p$, all other registers zero, and no answer set, to the configuration with state $mathrm{copy}(3,mathrm{false})$, the same pointer, query register $mathrm{bitsVal}(t)$, tail register $p$, all other registers zero, and no answer set. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the machine's safety condition and has each register at most $4|h|+4$. If either condition on $t$ fails, the machine instead halts with answer false from that initial configuration, with the same safety condition and register bound at every configuration before halting.
hypotheses_covered: Tail t is canonical and its length is at most the length of the binary representation of |h| in the reachability case
